grade.basis: Direct reading of the complete first-violin part, printed music pp.2–7. The Andantino already requires exposed high-register phrasing and rapid ornamental runs; the Allegro adds quick position changes, off-string articulation, rapid arco/pizzicato changes, artificial harmonics and octave-displaced runs. Sustained diploma-level solo control; exposed three-violin coordination supports level 7. Other two parts not inspected, so first violin is the best-supported hardest-part estimate.

findings.finding: Inspected the complete Kistner score: three staves throughout, contrasting Grave, Scherzo, Canzonetta, Giocoso and funeral-march/Presto finale; substantial passagework appears in all three parts. Checked 2026-10-28.

grade.basis: Direct reading of the complete score, printed pp.5–11. All three violins carry active passagework and exposed exchanges; first violin has the most persistent high writing, trills and leaps. Grave has rapid ornamental bursts, the scherzo needs crisp coordinated articulation, Giocoso has sustained active figurations, and the final Presto demands fast shared scales, string-specific colors and precise handoffs. At roughly 22 minutes, cumulative coordination and stamina justify diploma level 7.
